newsitem.title: USA: CDW Computer shares fall despite strong Q1.
newsitem.headline: CDW Computer shares fall despite strong Q1.

text.p: Shares of CDW Computer Centers Inc fell on Friday despite strong first quarter earnings as investors apparently focused on a decline in the computer direct marketer's average order size.

"Some people may have been concerned about some of the other operating trends in the quarter, but I think some people don't really understand what is taking place," Michael Rosen, an analyst with Blackford Securities, said of the drop in average order size. "The quarter they reported yesterday was very good."

After the market closed Thursday, CDW reported first quarter earnings of $0.52 a share, up from $0.26 a share last year. The earnings topped the analysts' consensus estimate of $0.47 a share, according to First Call.
But CDW shares fell as low as 40 on Friday, and were off 2-3/8 at 44-1/4 in afternoon trading.
CDW, based in Buffalo Grove, Ill., said Friday its average order size decreased in the first quarter, but lower computer and related equipment prices drove the number of sales higher.
"We had a decrease in the average order size which was offset because we had strong growth in customers served and orders processed," chief financial officer Harry Harczak said in an interview.
Harczak said CDW's growth in orders and customer base was its largest since the first quarter of 1995. The number of orders rose 48 percent versus last year and customers were up 36 percent.
He said the decrease in order size was the result of falling computer prices, which in the long run is positive for the company's sales.
"There have been price decreases, but those decreases have really helped to drive our volume," Harczak said. "Given our very low-cost operational structure, we're very well positioned."
CDW said it expects additional price cuts from manufacturers and anticipates further sales will be driven by those reductions.
The company said it will continue to expand its marketing and sales operations, and it is planning to move into its new expanded facility in July.

"CDW is a company whose strength in the past has not been marketing," Rosen said. "Lately they have really started to focus on that, and based on the performance in this quarter I think that's good news."

Harczak said the new facility costs CDW about $22 million to $25 million, but the costs are largely offset by the lack of leasing expenses. He said the facility is paid for from the company's cash reserves.
"It's pretty much a tradeoff, but we will have some additional costs," Harczak said. "We could see some slight increase, but I don't see anything material."
